analysis: The only changed file is docs/developer/build.md, a documentation-only change (base lines 162-167, head lines 162-184). It describes how scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh picks the Xcode/SDK: image Xcode first, then installed /Applications/Xcode*.app newest first, preferring SDK 27.2. An explicit DEVELOPER_DIR is the only candidate. It adds two modes via DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN: 'release' requires SDK 27.2 and Swift 6.4.2, 'qualification' accepts 27.2 or 27.0 with Swift 6.4/6.4.x. The signed-validation job on macOS-26 is described as running the signed app and compiling nothing. No code, runtime, protocol, key custody, attestation or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The text is relevant to the artifact and qualification contract (A-017, T-054, TB-011): it states that release evidence must use the selected release toolchain, and it keeps release mode stricter than qualification mode. The 27.0 allowance applies to the qualification mode used by CI and pull-request preparation, while master, dispatched and release workflows are documented as 'release' mode requiring 27.2. I could not verify that the script or workflows actually implement this split; they are not in the supplied units. Consumers of the selected toolchain, such as release-provider.yml and signing validation, were not supplied. A later pass on those files should confirm that the script enforces the documented mode defaults, that release workflows set 'release' explicitly, and that qualification-mode builds cannot be published. This documentation change itself introduces no concrete regression. I examined all three units: base chunks 1 and 2, and head chunk 1. The head chunk is truncated at line 487, so the end of the file is not visible on the head side.
